To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
food deprivation in cattle decreases circulating IGF-I and this decrease is associated with a decrease of IGF-I mRNA levels in the liver.
food deprivation decreases serum IGF-I and liver total IGF-1 and GHR mRNA levels in steers.

food deprivation decreased the levels of circulating IGF-I and total IGF-I and GHR mRNAs in the liver, which is associated with a decrease of the levels of individual GHR and IGF-I mRNA transcripts in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the food deprivation-induced suppression of circulating IGF-I.
the regulation of IGF-I and its receptor in the liver of cattle and provides a basis for understanding the mechanism of the nutritional regulation of IGF system in ruminants.
the mechanisms underlying food deprivation-induced decrease of circulating IGF-I and the role of liver as an important organ for IGF-I synthesis and secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

food deprivation decreases circulating IGF-I concentrations by decreasing liver IGF-I expression through a mechanism involving the coordinate downregulation of IGF-I mRNA expression and the downregulation of specific IGF-I mRNA isoforms and GHR mRNA isoforms.

food deprivation decreased circulating IGF-I concentrations by reducing the expression of different liver IGF-I variants, which was associated with a reduction in the expression of specific liver GHR mRNA variants.
the food deprivationinduced decrease in serum IGF-I concentrations in cattle is associated with a decrease at the level of transcription in the expression of both IGF-I and GHR in the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the food deprivation induced decrease in liver GHR and IGF-I mRNA expression is associated with the decrease of liver IGF-I secretion and circulating IGF-I levels.
food deprivation decreases circulating IGF-I by reducing the expression of IGF-I mRNA as well as GHR mRNA in cattle.
food deprivation decreases serum IGF-I, which in turn decreases the expression of IGF-I mRNA (both class 1 and 2) and GHR mRNA in cattle liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nutritional status can affect both the levels of IGF-I mRNA transcripts in the liver and the levels of GHR mRNA transcripts in the same organ.
food deprivation induces a decrease in circulating IGH-I, and this is associated with a coordinated decrease in the expression in different IGF-I and GHR mRNA variant in the liver.
the food deprivation- induced decrease in serum IGF-I concentrations in steers is not due to a decrease in the expression levels of IGF-I mRNA variant 1 in the liver.
